description: Root every test scratch directory in a repo-local, dot-prefixed, three-sided-ignored scratch root via one helper, migrate all 474 os.tmpdir rooting sites under test/ to derived zero in five fronts, and lock it with a falsifiable gate inside the check:all spine.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms `bun test` recursively searches the working directory for *.test.{ts,tsx,...} and friends, which is why a surviving fixture inside a non-dot scratch directory would be collected as a phantom test file. The page documents the recursive discovery but does NOT document any dot-directory exclusion, so the dot-prefix requirement (US-002 AC2) stays a pinning guard justified by the behavior measured on 2026-08-05, not by a documented Bun guarantee; the implementer must keep AC2 derived from the helper's own return value rather than from a doc citation. No breaking change or deprecation affects the helper, the gate, or `bun test <file>` filtering used by the oracles.

Verified remedy: add '--no-install' to both spawnSync argvs (control run: `bun --no-install ./probe.ts` -> `error: Cannot find package 'chalk'`, exits non-zero), which makes the guard real and earns the allowlist exception. userStories.title: CRITICAL: The exit-time reaper (process.on('exit', reapOwnDirectories)) never r…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts:90]: The exit-time reaper (process.on('exit', reapOwnDirectories)) never runs under `bun test`, the only runner the helper exists for, so US-002 AC4 ('The helper reaps its directories on process exit') is not actually delivered. Proven by minimal probe: a test file registering process.on('exit', () => console.error('EXIT-HOOK-FIRED')) prints nothing under `bun test` (bun 1.3.13), and a controlled measurement shows running one test file (test/orchestrator/handoff.test.ts) leaves 6 directories behind (.cam-test-tmp entry count 4754 -> 4760). The scratch root had accumulated 4754 directories / 29MB from the branch's own development. The AC's own oracle passes only because test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts:75 pins the behavior in a `bun -e` child process, a runtime where exit hooks DO fire, rather than in the test runner: the test is green while the behavior is broken. Consequences: (a) unbounded-within-the-1h-window scratch growth inside the repo, and (b) pruneStaleSiblings (the only surviving mitigation) pays a readdirSync + per-entry statSync over that growing set on every process start (measured 12.3ms readdir + 7.7ms stat at 4760 entries), re-creating inside the repo the very enumeration cost GOTCHA 12 says the helper exists to eliminate. Bun's documented mechanism for run-wide teardown is afterAll in a --preload / bunfig.toml preload file (https://bun.sh/docs/test/lifecycle); the fix must also make the reaper test exercise `bun test`, not `bun -e`.

userStories.title: WARNING: The GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES fence is delivered as a runtime process.en…
userStories.description: WARNING [test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts:86]: The GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES fence is delivered as a runtime process.env mutation, so it only reaches child processes that forward live process.env, while the branch simultaneously created the hazard it guards against (scratch dirs now sit inside the cam-cli git repo, where an unfenced upward search resolves cam-cli's own working tree). scripts/validate-agents-md.ts was patched with `env: process.env` for exactly this reason, but src/commands/sidecar.ts:3091/3184/3186/3188 still call Bun.spawnSync(['git', '-C', cwd, 'checkout', 'main' | 'checkout', '-B', ... | 'add' ... | 'commit' ...]) with no env option. Those paths are safe only because their sole test (test/sidecar-resolver-git.test.ts) git-inits its scratch dirs; a future test driving them with a non-initialized scratch cwd would silently run `git checkout main` against the real cam-cli working tree, and nothing in the diff (no gate, no test, no lint rule) guards that. A location-independent fence (e.g. a stub .git entry in SCRATCH_ROOT so the upward search always terminates regardless of env propagation) does not depend on every spawn site remembering to forward env.

userStories.title: Ignore the repo-local scratch root on all three sides
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need the scratch root ignored by this repo, by the shipped template, and by the embedded copy that `cam init` actually writes, so the first test run that uses it cannot dirty a working tree here or in a user's project.
acceptanceCriteria: Git ignores the scratch root in this repo, a throwaway git repo materialized with only templates/.gitignore also ignores it, and src/vendor/_generated.ts (what `cam init` really writes) carries the same rule, which only happens by running `bun run embed-vendor` and committing the generated file. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'set -e; git check-ignore -q .cam-test-tmp/probe/x; grep -q cam-test-tmp src/vendor/_generated.ts; T="$(mktemp -d)"; git init -q "$T"; cp templates/.gitignore "$T/.gitignore"; git -C "$T" check-ignore -q .cam-test-tmp/probe/x'] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05 running the exact command: exit 1 at the first clause, because `git check-ignore -q .cam-test-tmp/probe/x` exits 1 and `grep -c cam-test-tmp` returns 0 in each of .gitignore, templates/.gitignore and src/vendor/_generated.ts (none of the three sides carries the rule). The oracle deliberately leaves the mktemp directory behind and never uses rm -rf (CAM-507, GOTCHA 6).

The scratch-root rule text is byte-identical between .gitignore and templates/.gitignore, and non-empty on both sides, because scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh compares git check-ignore verdicts between the two files and turns any textual divergence into DIVERGE (GOTCHA 1). [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'set -e; a="$(grep -F cam-test-tmp .gitignore)"; b="$(grep -F cam-test-tmp templates/.gitignore)"; test -n "$a"; test "$a" = "$b"'] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05 running the exact command: exit 1, because under `set -e` the first grep finds no match and aborts (neither side carries the rule, so the equality clause is never reached vacuously).

PINNING GUARD (green on main by design, patterns.md:928, not a change detector): the gitignore-parity regression gate stays green after the rule lands on both sides. [oracle: named-command bun test test/check-gitignore-parity-script.test.ts] Measured GREEN on main 2026-08-05 (4 tests, 0 fail, 9 expect calls); no red sweep is required or possible for a stays-green guard.
The embedded vendor copy is regenerated and committed, so the drift gate is clean (GOTCHA 2). [oracle: named-command bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: named-command bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: named-command bun test]
The full quality spine is green (bun run check:all). [oracle: named-command bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: .gitignore, templates/.gitignore, src/vendor/_generated.ts (generated, do not hand-edit). Scratch root literal is `.cam-test-tmp` (fixed by the issue oracles). ADR-0014 ordering (GOTCHA 1): this story MUST land before any test writes into the root, otherwise the first run dirties the tree and trips the plan-preflight clean-tree guard. GOTCHA 2: templates/.gitignore is embedded; src/templates/embedded.ts special-cases the '.gitignore' key and the content `cam init` writes comes from src/vendor/_generated.ts, so editing the template without `bun run embed-vendor` + committing the generated file both ships a user project without the rule AND reds the embed-vendor gate inside check:all. Keep the two rule lines textually identical (same anchoring, same trailing slash); anchored (`/.cam-test-tmp/`) or unanchored both keep parity green as long as the two files agree byte-for-byte. Never use rm -rf in any step (GOTCHA 6, CAM-507): the mktemp dir in AC1 is left behind on purpose.

userStories.title: Add the single test-scratch helper with git ceiling and exit reaper
userStories.description: As a test author, I need one helper that creates every temporary directory under the repo-local scratch root, survives process.chdir, hides the cam-cli repo from git, and reaps itself on process exit, so no test ever roots a directory in the shared $TMPDIR again.
acceptanceCriteria: test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts exists exporting a single temp-directory creation function, the file references node:os on NO code line (comment lines are ignored by the purpose oracle so a header explaining 'never root in os.tmpdir, see CAM-503' cannot red a correct implementation, GOTCHA 4), and test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts pins the behavior against the real filesystem: the returned path is under the repo-local scratch root, stays under it after a process.chdir() out of the repo (dozens of tests chdir, so the root must derive from import.meta.dir and never from process.cwd()), and does not start with the os temp dir. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'set -e; test -f test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts; ! grep -nE "node:os" test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts | grep -vE "^[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(//|\*|/\*)" | grep -q .; bun test test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts'] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05: exit 1, because test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts does not exist (measured `test -f` exit 1). The leading `test -f` clause is what makes the negation non-vacuous: grep over a missing file exits 2 and the bare `!` would return 0.

PINNING GUARD / DESIGN RESTRICTION (patterns.md:928, deliberately not an assertion about new bun behavior): the first path segment of the helper's return, relative to the repo root, starts with a dot, and test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts asserts this by DERIVING the segment from the helper's own return value, never by comparing against a frozen literal. Justification measured 2026-08-05 and unchanged by this issue: bun's test discovery walks the cwd at startup and collects a *.test.ts left inside a gitignored directory WITHOUT a dot, but not inside a dot-prefixed one, so a fixture surviving an aborted run would become a phantom failing test on the next run. [oracle: named-command bun test test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05: exit 1, because the test file does not exist. The pinning-guard label applies to the invariant being frozen, not to the oracle's redness today.

The helper sets GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES pointing at the scratch root, and the helper test proves with a REAL git subprocess that `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from a scratch directory fails with 'not a git repository' instead of returning the cam-cli root. Without this, every test that shells out to git from its temp directory would silently operate on cam-cli's own working tree once the root becomes repo-local. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'set -e; test -f test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts; grep -q GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts; bun test test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts'] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05 running the exact command: exit 1 at the first clause (helper absent).

The helper reaps its directories on process exit, pinned behaviorally: test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts spawns a real child process that creates a directory through the helper, prints the path and exits, and the parent asserts the path is gone afterwards; any prune of older sibling scratch roots is bounded and failure-tolerant and never enumerates the shared $TMPDIR (GOTCHA 12). [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'set -e; test -f test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts; grep -q reaper test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts; bun test test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts'] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05 running the exact command: exit 1 at the first clause (helper absent; the helper test file that must name the reaper case does not exist either).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: named-command bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: named-command bun test]
The full quality spine is green (bun run check:all). [oracle: named-command bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts (new), test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts (new). One function only: it must also serve the async `await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(...)` sites in test/retry migrated by US-007, so do not add a second helper. Derive the root from import.meta.dir (never process.cwd(): dozens of tests chdir out of the repo mid-test). Ban on node:os is about CODE, not prose (GOTCHA 4); as a by-product the helper structurally cannot readdir $TMPDIR, which is what keeps the prune bounded (GOTCHA 12: in the observed state ls and find blew 30-120s timeouts). CRITICAL spelling constraint: the helper test needs tmpdir() only as a COMPARAND to prove the returned path is not under the os temp dir (GOTCHA 8), and it must NOT be written as `join(tmpdir()` in any form, because the tree-wide derived-zero oracle of US-007 and the durable gate of US-008 both key on that spelling; write it as a startsWith/negation against the bare call instead. Reaper via a process exit hook; keep it failure-tolerant so a half-removed directory never fails an unrelated test. scripts/file-size-budget.json may need a raise once helper imports land (GOTCHA 13); raising and committing it is normal hygiene, never a hook bypass. check:all here also runs biome lint, knip dead-code, file-size and the jscpd dup gate, so the new files must be clean under all four at the story that introduces them.

userStories.title: Add the deterministic tmpdir gate with falsifiability probe and empty allowlist mechanism
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a deterministic scan script, shaped like the existing test-sleeps gate, that flags any tmpdir call reaching a path construction under test/, proves it can go red, and ships a working-but-empty allowlist mechanism, so the migration cannot silently regress.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts exists with an exported pure scan function plus a CLI main, molded on scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts, running clean over the migrated tree; test/check-test-tmpdir.test.ts pins that it flags a tmpdir CALL reaching a path-construction site in every reachable form (the three spellings observed on main: the mkdtempSync form, the awaited mkdtemp form and the bare path-join form; plus the namespaced call, the template-literal interpolation form and the same-file aliased binding form), and that it does NOT flag a tmpdir reference used only as a comparand, which is exactly what the helper test needs to prove its returned path is not under the os temp dir (GOTCHA 8). [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'set -e; test -f scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts; grep -q "export function" scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts; bun scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts; bun test test/check-test-tmpdir.test.ts'] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05 running the exact command: exit 1 at the first clause, because scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts does not exist (measured `test -f` exit 1).

FALSIFIABILITY (mandatory: a gate never seen red is not a gate; probe safe by construction): planting a single rooting site in a synthetic test file inside a throwaway scan root turns the gate RED and its output NAMES the file, after which the gate is green again on the real tree. The probe operates entirely OUTSIDE the working tree, never appends a line to a versioned file and never runs git checkout -- <file>, so it cannot discard uncommitted work on a dirty tree; cleanup uses rm -f on two named files and rmdir on provably empty directories, never rm -rf (GOTCHA 5, GOTCHA 6). No literal count is compared anywhere in the probe. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'set -e; d="$(mktemp -d)"; mkdir -p "$d/test"; printf "%s\n" "const p = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));" > "$d/test/leak-probe.test.ts"; v=green; bun scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts "$d" > "$d/out.txt" 2>&1 || v=fired; test "$v" = fired; grep -q "leak-probe.test.ts" "$d/out.txt"; rm -f "$d/test/leak-probe.test.ts" "$d/out.txt"; rmdir "$d/test" "$d"; bun scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts'] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05 running the exact command: exit 1, and for the right reason, since bun answers `error: Module not found "scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts"`, so v becomes fired but the output never names leak-probe.test.ts and the grep clause fails. Requires the gate to accept an optional scan root in argv, defaulting to test/.

ALLOWLIST MECHANISM ready, real allowlist EMPTY in this issue: the gate carries an allowlist with a per-entry reason, and test/check-test-tmpdir.test.ts proves both halves with SYNTHETIC entries injected into the scan function, an entry matching an existing file suppresses that file's finding, and an entry matching no existing file makes the gate FAIL, so an allowlist cannot outlive its own justification. The real allowlist stays empty, verified derivedly and not by a frozen literal, because its only legitimate consumers are the PRODUCT leak-regression tests that belong to the sister issue. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'set -e; test -f scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts; bun test test/check-test-tmpdir.test.ts; ! bun scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts --print-allowlist | grep -q .'] Swept RED on main 2026-08-05 running the exact command: exit 1 at the first clause. The leading `test -f` is load-bearing: the final negation alone is VACUOUSLY GREEN on main (measured exit 0 when the script is missing).

The scan's alternate-form coverage is pinned by name in the gate's own test, not merely asserted in prose: test/check-test-tmpdir.test.ts contains the namespaced-call case alongside the template-literal and aliased cases. findings.text: Layer B oracle FAIL (US-007 AC1, US-008 AC3, US-008 AC5 all RED on the reviewer's independent re-run) for an exception that is not earned. US-R1-001 surrendered the PRD's headline tree-wide derived-zero property and opened the first ALLOWLIST entry in exchange for a guard that does not work at runtime. The comment at :28-37 and the ALLOWLIST reason in scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts:75-86 both claim that rooting in the real OS temp dir keeps the vendored smoke script 'outside any node_modules resolution chain', so a script that grew a third-party import would be caught. Direct probe says otherwise: `cd $(mktemp -d) && bun ./probe.ts` where probe.ts is `import c from "chalk"` prints RESOLVED-CHALK, because bun auto-install satisfies the import from ~/.bun/install/cache. The test spawns `spawnSync('bun', [scriptPath], { cwd: tmpDir })` at :59 and :86 with no --no-install and no env isolation, so that is the regime it actually runs in. The zero-dep invariant is therefore still silently unguarded, which is exactly what the round-1 CRITICAL said; only its location changed. Verified remedy: add '--no-install' to both spawnSync argvs (control run: `bun --no-install ./probe.ts` -> `error: Cannot find package 'chalk'`, exits non-zero), which makes the guard real and earns the allowlist exception. Full evidence in scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt PROBE C.

The allowlist staleness check cannot deliver US-008 AC3's stated invariant ('an allowlist cannot outlive its own justification') now that the allowlist actually holds an entry. findStaleAllowlistEntries only asserts that the entry's path exists in the scanned set, and scanForTmpdirRoots filters allowlisted paths out at line 216 BEFORE scanning them, so the scan never learns whether the entry suppressed a real finding. If test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts is later migrated onto createTestTmpdir, or its rooting line is simply deleted, the entry keeps matching an existing path, stays green, and permanently exempts that whole file from the gate with no signal. Make an entry that suppressed nothing a finding of its own (scan the allowlisted file too, and report the entry as stale when it produced zero suppressions), and pin it with a test alongside the two synthetic-entry tests at test/check-test-tmpdir.test.ts:126-143.

Doc drift caused by this branch: the direct-fix lane doc still describes the deterministic safety net as '14 gates', but US-009 added test-tmpdir as gate #15 (scripts/check-all.ts:181), and both gate-count freeze tests were bumped 14 -> 15 (test/check-all.test.ts:92, test/gates-manifest.test.ts:72). The prose is now factually wrong in an agent-facing command doc that exists specifically to justify the lane by the strength of that net. One-word fix; there is no templates/ mirror of this file to keep in sync.

The CLI main (optional argv scan root, --print-allowlist, the stderr message shape, the exit-1 path) still has no unit coverage; test/check-test-tmpdir.test.ts exercises only the two pure functions. It is currently pinned solely by the US-008 PRD oracles, which do not survive the branch. Carried over from round 1, still open.

NESTED_EXCLUDED_MARKERS matches '.cam-test-tmp' as a bare substring anywhere in the path, so a legitimately named file such as test/x.cam-test-tmp.test.ts would be silently dropped from the scan. Anchoring it as a path segment ('.cam-test-tmp/') would match the sibling TOP_LEVEL_EXCLUDED_DIRS convention. Carried over from round 1, still open.

helperPath is interpolated into a single-quoted import specifier inside a `bun -e` program string, so a checkout path containing an apostrophe breaks the test; JSON.stringify would make it robust. Related, line 129's expect(stderr).toBe('') is brittle to any incidental bun warning on stderr. Carried over from round 1, still open.

The codemod inserts the helper import into the pruned node:os import's slot, leaving the relative './helpers/test-tmpdir' import sandwiched between node: builtins across the ~190 migrated files (e.g. test/supervisor/backend-adapter.test.ts:14-16, test/install-sh.test.ts:17-19). Biome does not enforce import organization so nothing fails, but the ordering is inconsistent with the rest of the tree. Carried over from round 1, still open.

Now that ALLOWLIST is non-empty, running the gate against any scan root other than the repo root always fails on the dangling-entry check (the allowlisted path is not in that root's file set). The US-008 AC2 falsifiability probe still passes only because it greps for the planted filename rather than asserting the failure reason. Consider skipping the staleness check when an explicit scanRoot argument is given, so the probe path stays diagnostic.

createTestTmpdir() now runs at module top level, so merely importing this file creates a real directory and mutates process.env.GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES as an import side effect, where the previous join(tmpdir(), ...) was a pure string computation. Harmless today (the directory is reaped run-wide and the ceiling is only ever a strict ancestor of scratch dirs), but moving it inside a beforeAll would keep module load side-effect free.

docs/adr/0056 states 'There is no bunfig.toml today' as part of its consequences section; this branch introduces one. The ADR convention in scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md is explicit supersession, never rewriting, and the ADR's actual invariant (the coverage/test exit-code coupling) is untouched since the new bunfig carries no coverage threshold, so nothing needs editing now. Noted so a future coverage-threshold story does not read that line as still-current fact.
